races.title: State Senate, District 6
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Larry Stutts

top: Alabama Hospital Association Political Action Committee
money.note: Covers January 2023 on, primary and general. Party-committee lines are often in-kind staff and mail.
money.source: Alabama Fair Campaign Practices Act system, downloaded Nov 5, 2026

cands.bio: Republican state senator for Alabama's District 6 since 2014, after unseating incumbent Roger Bedford. A veterinarian by training and an OB/GYN physician, he opened Colbert OB/GYN in Sheffield in 1992. He lives in Tuscumbia.

controversies.text: In March 2015, Stutts filed a bill to repeal a law on minimum insured hospital stays after childbirth and a law on dense-breast-tissue notices. The stay law was named for a former patient who died in 1998. Her widower's malpractice suit was settled on confidential terms. Stutts withdrew the bill, saying it was unrelated to any patient case.

cands.gaps: We found no documented statements or actions by Stutts on data centers, development or growth, homestead property taxes, foreign or institutional ownership of land, police pay or pensions, or school vouchers and charters. His campaign site makes broad claims about voting for lower taxes and higher education spending but names no specific bills. The 2019 abortion vote comes from a Wikipedia summary, not an official record. Ballotpedia did not identify any endorsements for the 2026 race, and he did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey. We could not verify the settlement described in the Rose's Law item beyond one Wikipedia page.

qual.background: Alabama state senator since November 2014 (12 years, re-elected through 2026). Before that he was an OB/GYN physician and owner of Colbert OB/GYN since 1992, and earlier ran a veterinary practice.
qual.why: More than a decade of prior legislative service plus business ownership puts him in the high band. Committee seats and chairmanships were not counted.

pro-life.evidence: Voted in May 2019 for an Alabama bill making abortion a crime at any stage of pregnancy, with no exemptions for rape or incest (per Wikipedia; the roll call itself was not among the pages reviewed).

second-amendment.evidence: His campaign site says he does not support proposed gun control laws that would limit gun ownership for responsible, law-abiding citizens and will oppose any attempt to infringe that right.

workers-first.evidence: His campaign site lists 'stopping illegal immigration' among his priorities for families, with no specifics given.

school-choice-teachers.evidence: His campaign site says he voted to increase education funding and teacher salaries and supports 'parent-driven, child-centered education.' It does not mention vouchers or charters.

cands.name: Bobby Martin

money.note: Covers January 2023 on, primary and general. Party-committee lines are often in-kind staff and mail.
money.source: Alabama Fair Campaign Practices Act system, downloaded Nov 5, 2026

cands.bio: Bobby Wayne Martin Jr. is a pastor at Cowboy Church of Franklin County and lives in Tuscumbia. He says he previously worked in sales, factory jobs and design work. He has held no public office. He was the Democratic candidate for Alabama State Senate District 6 in 2026.

endorsements.text: Ballotpedia lists two voter-guide recommendations: Tabitha's List and Unburdening The Ballot (Sway voting groups). In his Ballotpedia survey he said he had not formally received or announced organizational endorsements.

cands.gaps: We could not find where Martin was born, where he grew up, or the year he first came to Alabama. He has held no public office, so there is no record of official actions. We found no stated positions from him on data centers, development or growth, land ownership by out-of-state or foreign buyers, immigration or H-1B, policing, guns, abortion, or school choice. His campaign site also mentions two years of free community college or trade training and no state income tax under $100,000, but we found nothing more detailed. We found no news coverage of controversies or foreign ties.

local.label: Roots 40: His campaign site says he and his wife have made Tuscumbia their home for 20 years, but his birthplace and childhood locations are not stated, so the score reflects about 20 years as an adult resident.

score.why: Raised $1,314, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Pastor of Cowboy Church of Franklin County, and earlier worked in sales, factory jobs and design work; no elected office, legislative, policy or budget experience is documented.
qual.why: His work history is in unrelated occupations and he has held no office, which fits the low range for a lawmaking and budget job.
